2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.headline: Missing 14-year-old autistic boy Ethan Boyd safely located, Martin County sheriff says
2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.teaser: Ethan Boyd, a missing 14-year-old autistic boy, was safely located at 11:44 p.m., according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.
2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.body:
The Martin County Sheriff’s Office had asked the public for help locating Ethan Boyd, a 14-year-old autistic boy who went missing Wednesday in Palm City. Ethan was last seen at 5:20 p.m. running toward the south side of the Grand Oaks senior living community near Coquina Cove.

Ethan was described as 5 feet 7 inches tall, weighing approximately 130 pounds, with brown hair. He was last seen wearing a dark blue shirt and seafoam green shorts without shoes.

The sheriff’s office asked anyone who saw Ethan to contact deputies immediately. The agency later updated its original Facebook post to announce that he had been safely located.
2026-08-06-martin-county-sheriffs-office.update_text: Ethan Boyd has been safely located, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office. The agency announced the update in its original Facebook post and thanked the public for sharing information about the missing teenager.

2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.headline: Florida executes 77-year-old Curtis Beasley, state's 16th this year
2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.teaser: Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, was executed by lethal injection Tuesday evening at Florida State Prison and pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m.
2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.body:
Florida executed Curtis Wilkie Beasley on Tuesday evening at Florida State Prison, where the 77-year-old was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. following a lethal injection. Beasley became the 16th person executed by Florida in 2026.

Beasley was convicted of first-degree murder, robbery and grand theft auto in the 1995 killing of Carolyn Monfort. Prosecutors said he beat Monfort with a hammer at her home, stole money and her vehicle, and later was arrested in Alabama while using a false identity.

The Florida Supreme Court and U.S. Supreme Court rejected last-minute efforts to stop the execution. His attorneys had argued, among other claims, that executing him at age 77 while experiencing cognitive decline would violate constitutional protections.

Beasley was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. Tuesday, according to state officials.
2026-09-29-florida-executes-77-year-old-.update_text: Florida executed Curtis Wilkie Beasley Tuesday evening. He was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. following a lethal injection at Florida State Prison.

2026-10-09-port-st-lucie-police-seek-hel.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Eric Saint Aude in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run
2026-10-09-port-st-lucie-police-seek-hel.teaser: Port St. Lucie police identified Eric Saint Aude, 60, as the driver arrested in the October 9 hit-and-run that critically injured a 63-year-old man. Investigators are still seeking a second vehicle.
2026-10-09-port-st-lucie-police-seek-hel.body:
Police said the collision occurred at about 12:56 a.m. October 9 near Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard. A 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man was found unconscious with serious head injuries and bleeding. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said at the October 23 briefing that the man remained in critical condition and had not yet been able to describe what happened.

Detectives reviewed surveillance video, vehicle debris and other evidence to locate the driver. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant helped lead investigators to Saint Aude and a vehicle associated with the crash. Detectives took Saint Aude into custody at his home and obtained the vehicle, which police said had damage consistent with a pedestrian collision. Investigators planned additional testing of possible blood evidence found on the vehicle.

According to Niemczyk, Saint Aude was on his way to pick up newspapers for delivery when the collision occurred. Investigators allege he left the scene without stopping, rendering aid or reporting the crash. The charge is an allegation; the filing of a criminal charge does not establish guilt.

Investigators believe a second vehicle may have been present at the time of the crash, with one vehicle traveling northbound and another southbound. Police are seeking the southbound vehicle or its driver, who may have additional information about what happened. Police have not established in the public statements reviewed that the second vehicle also struck the pedestrian.
2026-10-09-port-st-lucie-police-seek-hel.update_text: Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk identified Eric Saint Aude, 60, of Port St. Lucie, as the arrested driver in the Oct. 9 hit-and-run. Police said Saint Aude was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

2026-10-26-coastal-flood-warning-covers-.first_paragraph: A coastal flood warning remains in effect for coastal St. Lucie County until 2 a.m. Thursday, October 29, as king tides and rough surf raise the risk of significant flooding along Florida’s Atlantic coast. The National Weather Service warns that high water could inundate low-lying roads and waterfront properties around high tide, especially where drainage is poor. Residents should avoid flooded roads and follow local safety advisories.

2026-10-29-one-hospitalized-after-rollov.body:
One person was taken to a hospital after a single-vehicle rollover on SW Martin Highway in Martin County on Thursday, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.

The crash occurred west of Fox Brown Road. Deputies and emergency personnel responded, and the sheriff’s office warned motorists to expect delays while the scene was cleared.
